followup_explanation:
I weighed two things in the documentation:

1. **Capability fit.** Your question is an open-ended, explanatory "explain the causes of X" request that draws on broad world knowledge and reasoning. Willet scores meaningfully higher on the benchmarks most relevant to that — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 56.2), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2). Those gaps are well outside the noted run-to-run variance, so they're real.

2. **Task preference.** Lapwing self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative work and prefers tightly-scoped retrieval/extraction/reformatting tasks. Your question is the opposite of that — broad and latitude-heavy. Willet has near-zero preference slopes on this kind of task, so no aversion either way.

Both point the same direction, so Willet was the clear pick.

One honest caveat: the documentation notes that Lapwing's *measured capability* on creative/open-ended work is actually strong despite its stated dislike of it — preference and quality are dissociated. So Lapwing wouldn't have done a bad job. But since Willet wins on the head-to-head capability evals *and* has no preference friction, it was still the better routing choice.
